summary.name: Production is all that matters
summary.one_liner: A blog essay arguing developers must observe and handle how their software behaves in production, covering logging, alerting, statistics, and fault-tolerant code.
use_cases: Setting up application logging for production debugging
Writing retry logic for flaky third-party APIs
Adding monitoring scripts that check data invariants
Tracking application statistics like error counts and purchases
Improving developer ownership of production systems
summary.what_it_does: The essay explains why production behavior matters more than code elegance and defines production, access, and error. It describes three developer-facing output streams: application logs (with timestamp, severity, process and request identifiers), alerting (push notifications for actionable events, with catch-all exception handlers and invariant-checking scripts), and application statistics (vital-sign metrics tracked over time, with Graphite and Statsd mentioned). It then covers how to fix production errors immediately and how to make code fault-tolerant, using a Ruby background-job retry example and rules of thumb about third-party calls.
notable: Includes Ruby code examples for retrying a charge job and wrapping save! errors with context
Recommends the book Release It! by Michael Nygard
Promotes the author's book The Senior Software Engineer at $25
caveats: Opinion essay rather than a software tool; examples are Ruby/Rails-specific
Mentions a paid book by the author ($25)
